history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: actual town is Sivanmalai, a hill village near Kangayam, about 35 km from Tiruppur (not Tiruppur itself). Legend: when Shiva used Mount Meru as his bow against the Asuras' Tripura, the bow's tip broke off and fell to earth, becoming this hill. Parvathi performed penance here (hence 'Shakthi/Sakthimalai'); the sage Agastya created a Ganga-water spring on Karthigai Pournami; Hanuman worshipped here after being directed by sage Vyasa; Valli did penance here before Murugan brought her and later Deivanai to reside here. The hill is also called Panamalai, Vellimalai, Sembumalai in earlier yugas and Kamarupa Jothigiri in Kali Yuga (legendary names, no dated epigraphic evidence cited). Templenet notes rule by Kongu chieftains until the 13th century, then Vijayanagara and Madurai Nayaks. Celebrated in Arunagirinathar's Tiruppukazh and other Tamil devotional literature. Monthly Karthigai asterism and new-moon days are special at this temple.
